Playbook.name: AD — New Computer (Machine) Account Created - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A computer account was created (4741). Most are legitimate device joins, but attackers create machine accounts for persistence and for attacks like noPac/sAMAccountName spoofing and RBCD. Triage question: was this a normal domain-join by a provisioning/admin path, or an unexpected principal minting a machine account?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Attacker-controlled computer accounts enable resource-based delegation abuse and blend into normal AD noise.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Bulk device provisioning via SCCM/Intune/join account is routine; a normal user account creating a machine account (default MachineAccountQuota=10 lets any user do this) is the abuse shape.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the creator is an approved device-provisioning path and whether the new account shows abuse (rename, delegation, immediate ticket).

Step.name: Creator identity and creation rate
Step.Purpose: A designated join/provisioning account creating machines is normal; a regular USER creating one (MAQ abuse) stands out.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4741" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS created = COUNT(*), machines = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | SORT created DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Provisioning accounts create many; a human user with 1 creation stands out. A user creating several machine accounts quickly is noPac/RBCD-style setup.

Step.name: Was the new machine account renamed or delegated right after (4742)
Step.Purpose: Immediate 4742 changes to the new account (sAMAccountName rename, msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOf) are the noPac/RBCD tells.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4742" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName, winlog.event_data.SamAccountName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A rename (SamAccountName dropping the trailing $) or msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity being set immediately after creation is strong RBCD/noPac evidence.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a NON-provisioning user creating the machine account, especially several, or INV-02 shows immediate rename/delegation changes.
INV-01 shows a designated join/provisioning account (SCCM/Intune/domain-join service) creating the account normally.
Creator is a helpdesk/admin user with device-join rights and no follow-on manipulation - routine but unticketed.
Creator role unclear and no manipulation yet.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-MACH-CREATE, INV-02-MACH-MANIP to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Normal device onboarding via an approved provisioning identity.

Indicators.Item: Creator is the domain-join/SCCM/Intune service or a device admin.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the device-join workflow; close as false_positive/benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: Attacker created a machine account for delegation abuse or persistence.

Indicators.Item: Regular user creating machine account(s) (MAQ abuse).
Immediate rename (noPac) or RBCD delegation set.
New account used to obtain tickets.

SOCAction.Item: Investigate the creator's session; open IR.
Set MachineAccountQuota to 0 and delegate joins properly.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An automation creating computer objects unexpectedly (staging/imaging job misfire).

Indicators.Item: Provisioning account creating extras due to a broken job.

SOCAction.Item: Clean up stray objects; fix the job.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If abuse indicators: disable the new machine account; identify the creator's session.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Hunt for RBCD delegation and ticket requests using the account; remove delegation.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Set MachineAccountQuota=0; delegate machine creation to provisioning accounts only.

QualityChecks.Check: 4741 is high-volume-benign in most estates - rely on creator identity + 4742 follow-on, not the creation alone.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Approved provisioning path confirmed; no manipulation.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Rogue account removed; creator investigated; MAQ hardened.
